text: The propositional truncation ‖A‖₋₁ of A satisfies: ‖A‖₋₁ is inhabited if and only if A is inhabited.
explanation: ‖A‖₋₁ comes with |·|: A → ‖A‖₋₁, so if A is inhabited, so is ‖A‖₋₁. Conversely, ‖A‖₋₁ is a mere proposition, so to map out of it into a proposition P, you need a map A → P (not an element of A directly).
